newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Trend not debt level crucial for EMU entry - Portugal.
newsitem.headline: Trend not debt level crucial for EMU entry - Portugal.

text.p: Portugal and Spain are committed to joining a European single currency in the first wave, Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said on Saturday.

But he said that a large number of founding group countries would not reach the target celing for entry of a debt to GDP ratio of 60 percent and would have to be included on the basis that their debt ratio was declining.

Guterres, speaking after a meeting of European socialist leaders taking part in a European Union summit later on Saturday, said, "I met the Spanish Prime Minister (Jose Maria Aznar) this weekend. It is a very strong commitment of both governments, both countries, to join a single European currency at the beginning.
"We are doing everything that is required for that and we are doing it in a very determined way."

He said that Portugal would meet the deficit criterion for entry into a single currency. It would not achieve the debt criterion in 1997, the year which will be considered in deciding which countries qualify for EMU, but debt would be declining as a proportion of GDP.

"Some of the countries which will surely be with the founding members will not have the 60 percent of GDP debt (ratio) -- Belgium (for example)...I cannot see a single currency without Belgium. If you want to include Belgium, you have to look at debt as a tendency, not as a fixed level."
